teams.synopsis: The team to beat for 2023 — an unparalleled RB duo and barely a real weakness anywhere.
teams.blurb:
• 2nd most points in week 1
  • Unparalleled RB duo, top 3-5 QB, a top 10 WR, and top 3 TE
  • No real holes in this team besides maybe the WR2 and the bench

This looks like the team to beat for the 2023 PFFL season, barring any injuries. Carmine's RB duo is made up of two potential top-5 guys, but that doesn't mean the rest of his team is weak. He has some strong fantasy producers, like Josh Allen and CeeDee Lamb. However, if there were any flaws within this squad, it would be the potential issues found within his WR2 and FLEX spots.

teams.synopsis: The most points in Week 1, but a heavy defensive contribution raises real fluke questions.
teams.blurb:
• Put up the most points in week 1, but defense contributed 30+ so it doesn't matter
  • No real holes besides RB2
  • Good bench depth, but questions around if the performances were a fluke

A great and balanced starting lineup can be just enough for this team to be a powerhouse for the 2nd straight year, but I wonder if the good performances in week 1 were just flukes. The average bench gives some flexibility on the trade front, but I don't know what trades can be made to retain value.

teams.synopsis: A tough loss, but a top-3-points week says this team deserves more respect.
teams.blurb:
• RB duo still very weak, but proved they can be good enough to put up a combined 25+
  • Burrow had a bad week 1, so I expect him to bounce back in week 2, and same goes for Waddle — not as bad as week 1 but still
  • Bench depth is very solid; Love can be Burrow's replacement if needed

It hurts my soul to put Brandon this high, but it's the respect he deserves. He lost this past week, but I think he proved that he's a top team in the PFFL. Yes, a couple of his WRs overperformed, but at the same time his QB put up 3.2 and he still put up the 3rd-highest points in the league. Keep an eye on Brandon to be a contender in 2023.

teams.synopsis: The RB trio looked like the real deal — a top TE or WR2 is the last piece needed.
teams.blurb:
• RB trio of Walker, Jones, and Hall looked like the real deal
  • Lost QB1 but has some solid plug-in options in Howell and Purdy
  • WR2 is biggest hole in lineup, but trades to fix that could be difficult with a mid-bench

I still am not sure what will happen with Taylor, but I don't know how much his absence will affect this team. Ryan's team has the potential to be a perennial top-5 team, even with the injuries and missing players, but I do think he needs either a top TE or solid WR2 to be considered a threat to all.

teams.synopsis: A risky roster, but the proof is in the pudding — 109 points with the WRs underperforming.
teams.blurb:
• Potential top 3 RB duo in the league, but the WR corps lacks
  • Bench has a couple solid young players
  • Can be very good, but one of the riskiest teams in the league

I understand if people may discredit this team as being #5, but the proof is in the pudding. Quin was able to put up 109 points in a win even though his WRs underperformed and his RB2 and FLEX put up 14.7 combined. I think this team has the potential to be really good, but that also depends on whether these bad performances were flukes and if Ekeler can stay healthy.

teams.synopsis: All the pieces of a powerhouse — we've seen flashes, now they just need to put it together.
teams.blurb:
• No holes in his lineup, except unproven FLEX
  • Mediocre bench limits trade flexibility
  • Can easily be a top 3 team

Cole's team has all the pieces it needs to be a powerhouse, but that depends on how consistent and productive his elite players are. If Henry and Javonte can both be top 15, and Hurts can return to his MVP form, while his WR duo of ARSB and Allen can put up 15+ each week, this team will be the team to beat. We've seen flashes, now they just need to put it all together.

teams.synopsis: A dip this week, but a top-5 team by Week 2 looks very possible.
teams.blurb:
• No real weakness in this lineup, besides the TE and no elite RB
  • Had a solid week but can still do so much better
  • Strong bench with Montgomery and Collins

Deniz dropped this week, but I can see him bouncing back up to the top 5 by Week 2. There are many pieces on this team that have the potential to be great undervalued players this year, like Montgomery, Collins, and Tua. If this team can play to its potential and his players stay healthy, then Deniz can be a top team for the 2023 PFFL season.

teams.synopsis: An embarrassing week with two zeroes is unlikely to repeat — the bench depth says a trade is coming.
teams.blurb:
• Has a lot of mid RBs that won't win him weeks but will lose them
  • Poor TE and WR play last week left him with an embarrassing loss
  • Potentially the best bench in the league

Even though Anthony lost to Charlie this week, I am ranking him higher because of the pure value of players on this team. Two players put up 0.0 for Anthony in Week 1, which is something I think won't happen again. I believe a trade for this team is coming because of the bench depth, but we shall see what happens.

teams.synopsis: Injuries could sink an early record, but a full-strength version of this team is dangerous.
teams.blurb:
• Weak TE and RB2 land this team in the #9 spot
  • Solid bench with the likes of Kyren Williams and Kamara
  • Injuries might limit this team's success

Diontae and Kamara being out for the next few weeks may cause this team to go 1-2 or even 1-3 to begin the season. However, when this team is at full strength and Tyreek is doing Tyreek things, then I think this team can be great.

teams.synopsis: A team built entirely around Kupp's health — not scary, but solid when full strength.
teams.blurb:
• Weak TE and no real superstar since Cooper Kupp is on IR
  • Solid bench with one of Mostert, Watson, or Pickens being forced to the bench
  • Loss of Kupp limits ceiling, but if he returns Ben can be solid

Ben's team is very well balanced but not in the best way possible. It has many good players at every position, except TE, but no real elite fantasy players on the roster besides Cooper Kupp. If Kupp returns to playing by midseason, then I think Ben can be a playoff team that can make some noise.

teams.synopsis: A win this week, but a bottom-5 roster underneath it — the holes need trades to fix.
teams.blurb:
• No real superstar on this team this past week, might change with Kelce
  • Loss of RB2 for the season leaves this team rather weak at RB
  • Extremely weak bench, besides Meyers

Even though Aidan won this past week, I believe that his team is bottom 5. If Dak, McLaurin, and Lockett don't get better, then I fear that this team will be in contention for #14 on next week's list. There are many holes within the lineup and no real players stand out, so I think this team will be limited to a non-playoff team if no trades are made.

teams.synopsis: Stuck waiting on health and form — a good #12, but the floor next week could be #14.
teams.blurb:
• Disappointing week from QB, WRs, and TE led to a ten-point loss
  • If Jeudy and Gainwell are healthy, then this team has potential to bounce back
  • Solid bench, but not great

Root's team is kind of just stuck — he's left waiting to see if players are healthy or if other players will perform to their ADP, but at the same time I wonder if players like Gainwell, Beckham, Goedert, and Burks have any value on the open market. #12 is a good spot for this team, but I think their floor for next week is #14, while still having a limited ceiling.

teams.synopsis: A fresh trade might turn this team around — but losing Rodgers caps Wilson's ceiling.
teams.blurb:
• Very weak RB duo, while the WR duo has potential to be one of the best in the league
  • Has DJ Moore/Mike Williams as a bench value or a potential trade piece
  • The trade that was just made might turn this team around a little

This team has some great potential to be a solid playoff team, but the loss of Rodgers might limit Wilson to an at-most WR10 season. I think that Max's team doesn't scare many in the league, but I do think with the right luck this team can make a strong push for and within the playoffs.

teams.synopsis: A potential league-record-low week drops this team to last by default.
teams.blurb:
• Questions surrounding every position except his RB1
  • Some of the worst bench depth in the league
  • The WRs are likely to be much better in the future

Although Baylen has some fantasy stars on his team, like Fields and Chase, he put up a potential league-record low for points in a week. I have no choice but to rank this team last by default for that reason, but I would have put them #14 anyway because this team has almost no flexibility with a mediocre bench as of now.
